extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners, patent practitioners (attorneys/agents) and applicants
extracted.subtask_short: USPTO patent examination and prosecution guidelines
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural standards from the MPEP describing substantive and procedural requirements for examination, restriction/election/rejoinder practice, appeals, reissue, classification, IFW processing, and related PTO petitions and forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality statement for environment/energy petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application disclosure is not clear on its face that the claimed invention materially enhances the quality of the environment or materially contributes to the conservation of energy, the petition must be accompanied by a statement explaining how the materiality standard is met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also revised to indicate that no fee is required for a petition under 37 CFR 1.102 based on the reason that the invention materially contributes to countering terrorism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental reply entry during suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: A supplemental reply will be entered if it is filed within the period during which action is suspended by the Office under 37 CFR 1.103(a) or 1.103(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental replies are not entered as a matter of right unless filed during such suspension periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express abandonment to avoid publication
rubrics_metrics.description: A letter of express abandonment or a petition under 37 CFR 1.138(c) for express abandonment to avoid publication may be mailed or faxed to the Office or faxed to the Pre-Grant Publication Division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a letter of express abandonment is submitted after payment of the issue fee, it must be accompanied by a petition to withdraw from issue under 37 CFR 1.313(c) and the appropriate fee; the petition is not effective unless received and granted before the date of issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of previously mailed correspondence (37 CFR 1.8(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.8(b) permits applicant to notify the Office of a previous mailing or transmission of correspondence and submit a statement under 37 CFR 1.8(b)(3) accompanied by a duplicate copy of the correspondence when a reasonable amount of time has elapsed from the time of mailing or transmitting the correspondence without having to wait until the application becomes abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms PTO/SB/64, PTO/SB/64A, PTO/SB/64/PCT, PTO/SB/61, PTO/SB/61/PCT, PTO/SB/62, and PTO/SB/63 updated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary amendment as part of original disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed on or after September 21, 2004, a preliminary amendment that is present on the filing date of the application is part of the original disclosure of the application; for applications filed prior to that date, a preliminary amendment present on the filing date is part of the original disclosure only if the preliminary amendment was referred to in the first executed oath or declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also: an amendment canceling claims to reduce excess claims fees should be filed before the expiration of the time period set forth in the notice that requires the excess claims fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of excess claims fee payment for newly added excess claims
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicant adds a new excess claim that is in excess of the number of claims that were previously paid for (after taking into account claims that have been canceled), applicant must pay the required excess claims fees before the examiner considers the new claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures fees are paid prior to substantive consideration of newly-added excess claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of amendments received after notice of allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: If an amendment is filed prior to the mailing of a notice of allowance, but is received by the examiner after the mailing of the notice of allowance, the amendment may not be approved for entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Added examples of amendments by applicant after allowance which must comply with 37 CFR 1.312. If an amendment under 1.312 does not comply with 1.121 and entry of the amendment would have been otherwise recommended, the examiner may enter the amendment and correct the non-compliance using an examiner's amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telegraphic amendment practice deleted
rubrics_metrics.description: The section on 'telegraphic amendment' has been deleted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of affidavits under 37 CFR 1.132
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples added to illustrate when an affidavit submitted under 37 CFR 1.132 is considered to be timely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides concrete timing examples to determine whether affidavits are timely filed to overcome rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of related, independent, and distinct inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarified when two or more inventions are 'related' and the meaning of 'independent' and 'distinct.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in restriction practice and to determine appropriate examination scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction definition and practice clarified
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised to clarify the definition of 'restriction' and the grounds and form for making a restriction requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every requirement to restrict should set forth why each invention as claimed is independent or distinct from the other(s), and why there would be a serious burden on the examiner if restriction is not required; examiner must establish burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markush-type claim guidance and provisional election of species
rubrics_metrics.description: Added explanation of what a Markush-type claim is, clarified when the provisional election of a single species is given effect, and clarified when a second action on a Markush-type claim can be made final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses treatment of multi-species chemical/genus claims and elections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nucleotide sequences and rejoinder consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Defined what is meant by 'nucleotide sequences' in context and clarified when rejoinder should be considered for sequence claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double patenting for joint research agreement inventions (CREATE Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporated discussion of double patenting between non-commonly owned inventions resulting from activities undertaken within the scope of a joint research agreement pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 103(c) as amended by the CREATE Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revised charts overviewing treatment of conflicting claims; added information regarding terminal disclaimers where conflicting applications resulted from joint research agreements; discussed timing of double patenting rejections when a reference relied upon in a 103(a) rejection may be disqualified under 103(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment when provisional double patenting rejection is sole remaining rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised procedure to be followed if a 'provisional' double patenting rejection is the only rejection remaining in an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charts and procedural steps updated to address finality and applicant responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejoinder practice and criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Rewritten to set forth general information pertaining to reconsideration of the propriety of a restriction requirement and rejoinder of certain previously nonelected inventions upon the determination that (1) all claims directed to the elected invention are in condition for allowance, and (2) claims to the previously nonelected invention depend from or otherwise require all the limitations of an allowable claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any claims are rejoined, the restriction requirement between the elected invention and rejoined invention(s) must be withdrawn. Rejoinder between product inventions and between process inventions discussed; rejoinder of processes requiring an allowable product only if all claims to the elected product invention are allowable and all process claims subject to rejoinder depend from or otherwise require all the limitations of an allowable product claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation of nonelected claims before allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application is in condition for allowance but for the presence of claims drawn to invention(s) nonelected without traverse, the claims drawn to the nonelected invention(s) may be canceled by examiner's amendment unless those claims are eligible for rejoinder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should determine if any allowable claims are linking or generic, or if any nonelected invention is eligible for rejoinder, before canceling claims drawn to the nonelected invention(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to establish burden for restriction between independent inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner must establish burden in order to restrict between either independent or distinct inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The restriction requirement should state why each invention is independent or distinct and why a serious burden on the examiner would result without restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election of species: reasoning and identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Election of species or restriction practice for species requires reasons for independence or distinctness, and reasons why examination of the claimed or disclosed species would be burdensome if election of species practice were not required. A restriction requirement must identify the species from which an election is to be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph revisions (e.g., 8.22) provide additional guidance concerning requirement for election and means for traversal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner may require later election single species
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may require an applicant to elect a single species upon later presentation of claims to more than one patentably distinct species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must make his/her own election; practice clarified regarding requirement for election and traversal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking claims and rejoinder between linked inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarified definition of 'linking claim' and explained that linking claims and the inventions they link together are usually either all directed to products or all directed to processes; provided examples and limitations of linking claims for rejoinder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provided reference to rejoinder sections for product or process inventions and clarified that rejoinder applies to claims which require all the limitations of an allowable claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction requirement outline
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised to set forth the outline that should be used to set forth a restriction requirement, whether between independent or related inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures consistent, detailed record explaining reasons for restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals: ex parte appeal structure and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Chapter revisions reflect new Part 41 Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences rules and add sections addressing composition of the Board, administrative handling, notice of appeal, reinstatement of appeal, and that an applicant cannot file an appeal in a continuation or an RCE until the application is under a rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms PTO/SB/31 and PTOL-461 updated; see MPEP § 2674–2683 for inter partes reexamination appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal brief timing and content
rubrics_metrics.description: New sections discuss time for filing the appeal brief and the content required in the appeal brief; rules on non-compliant appeal briefs and amended briefs added.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms PTOL-462 and PTOL-462R updated; form paragraphs revised; see 37 CFR 41.37 and related rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments, affidavits, and evidence filed with/after appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Discusses amendments and affidavits or other evidence filed with or after appeal and references new appeal rule 37 CFR 41.33.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If prosecution was reopened prior to a Board decision, fees paid for notice of appeal/brief/oral hearing will be applied to a later appeal on the same application; increased fees differences may be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's answer and new grounds of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: New section added to discuss contents of the examiner's answer and requirements for a new ground of rejection, including situations where new grounds are not permitted, requests for designation as a new ground, and appellant’s reply to new grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referenced new appeal rules (e.g., 37 CFR 41.39, 41.43).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reopening prosecution after appeal and remand practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Reopening of prosecution after appeal and remand by the Board for further consideration of rejections, amendment, affidavits/declarations, or further search is addressed; remand for further search should be extremely rare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where an affidavit or declaration is filed after notice of appeal but before Board decision, the examiner is without authority to consider it unless the examiner determines it overcomes all rejections under appeal and there is good and sufficient reason why it was not earlier presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: At the oral hearing, appellant may only rely on evidence that has been previously entered and considered by the primary examiner and present arguments that have been relied upon in the brief or reply brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Added discussion as to when a request for an oral hearing is improper; form paragraphs revised; referenced 37 CFR 41.35 and related rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for rehearing limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments not raised in the briefs before the Board and evidence not previously relied upon in the brief and any reply brief are not permitted in the request for rehearing except (A) upon a showing of good cause, appellant may present a new argument based upon a recent relevant decision of the Board or a Federal Court, and (B) new arguments responding to a new ground of rejection made under 37 CFR 41.50(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request for rehearing by the examiner must state with particularity the points believed to have been misapprehended or overlooked; if approved by Deputy Commissioner for Patent Examination Policy, TC will mail a copy to the appellant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of Board decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Board decision is available for public inspection if rendered in a file open to the public; if rendered in a file not open to the public, the Director may publish the decision or make it available for public inspection when special circumstances warrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referenced 37 CFR 41.6 and related rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and procedures for judicial review and 35 U.S.C. 145
rubrics_metrics.description: Updated addresses for filing requests for extension of time to seek judicial review and mailing address for notice of appeal to the Federal Circuit; revised to indicate that all the expenses of the 35 U.S.C. 145 proceeding must be paid by the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: IFW (Image File Wrapper) processing and public PAIR access
rubrics_metrics.description: Added references and discussion regarding IFW processing and indicated that the general public can view the entire content of an IFW application file history by way of Public PAIR via the USPTO Internet site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pertains to scanning of foreign patent documents and NPL, handling replacement drawings after allowance, and IFW processing in reissue and other chapters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification system and examiner duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Updated information that the U.S. Patent Classification System index, class/subclass definitions, and related resources are available online; examiners' procedures for transferring applications between art units, assignment disputes, and Inter-TC Classification Dispute Resolution Procedures added.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should make an inventor's name search; for national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371 examiners will consider documents cited in the international search report when copies are present; various internal TC procedures and forms updated or deleted (e.g., PTO-447A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue application filing and amendment practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Revisions indicate when a petition for an unintentionally delayed benefit claim under 37 CFR 1.78(a)(3) is required in a reissue application; a reissue application can be granted a filing date without the basic filing fee, search fee, or examination fee; physical surrender of the original patent is no longer required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirement for a copy of each U.S. patent or publication listed in an IDS eliminated unless required; broadened claims may be presented after the two-year period even though different; inventor consent requirements for deleting inventors clarified; forms updated (PTO/SB/50, PTO/SB/51, PTO/SB/52, PTO/SB/55 deleted where unnecessary).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue fees and maintenance fee issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised to add discussion regarding the basic reissue application filing fee, search fee, examination fee, excess claims fees, application size fee, and issue fee; added subsection to address payment of maintenance fees where the patent has been reissued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTO/SB/56 updated; amended 37 CFR 1.178(a) applies retroactively to all pending applications; surrender of the original patent is automatic upon grant of the reissue patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue and interferences / ex parte reexamination interplay
rubrics_metrics.description: Added reference to new interference rules and revised to indicate that pursuant to 37 CFR 41.202(c), an examiner may require a reissue applicant to add a claim to provoke an interference, unless the reissue applicant cannot present the added claim; if a reissue is filed while the original patent is in an interference proceeding, the reissue applicant must promptly notify the Board within 20 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where reissue application merged with ex parte reexamination, the merged proceeding will not be stayed where there is litigation; examiner should inform TC SPRE if multiple reissue applications or reexamination pending for same patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deletion/movement of obsolete paper-file procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Many sections discussing paper file wrappers, ordering soft copies of patents, marking examiner’s copies, and maintaining paper search files have been deleted or moved, reflecting the move to electronic IFW and online resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms and sections updated accordingly; examiners should use online tools (EAST/WEST, Classification Home Page, Patent Examiner’s Toolkit).
